topics.label: Introduction and lecture overview
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic provides introductory framing and outlines the lecture's focus on the initiation and resolution of inflammation.

topics.label: Principles of innate immune recognition
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics establish the foundational concepts of how the innate immune system detects infection and cellular damage through molecular patterns and germline-encoded receptors.

topics.label: Pattern recognition receptor families and inflammasome pathways
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics examine the specific sensor systems that detect danger, detailing Toll-like receptors, cytosolic receptor families, and inflammasome activation cascades.

topics.label: Inflammatory mediator responses, leukocyte recruitment, and systemic pathology
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics describe how innate immune activation drives local cellular recruitment, adaptive priming via lymphatics, and severe systemic complications like sepsis.

topics.label: Resolution of inflammation, tissue repair, and chronic outcomes
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explain how the body terminates acute inflammation, restores damaged tissues, and adapts to persistent irritants through chronic inflammation and granuloma formation.

topics.label: Lecture conclusion
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic provides closing framing and announces the topic of the upcoming lecture.
